_comment: Laser and scan-path timing for AMB2018-01, transcribed from Heigel et al. 2020, J. Res. NIST 125:125005 (doi 10.6028/jres.125.005), Tables 2-5, Figs 7-8 and Secs 3.4.1-3.4.5. Values are as printed; nothing is inferred except where marked source_class=inferred.

source.paper: Heigel, Lane, Levine, Phan, Whiting (2020) JRES 125:125005
source.measurement_method: laser on/off command signal recorded at 200 MHz with a Nicolet Odyssey XE oscilloscope for select layers; infill timings measured on layer 3 of a trial build and assumed constant for layers 1-250
source.applies_to: both IN625 and 15-5 builds (paper states timing was the same for both materials)

laser_spot.note: vendor-supplied nominal Gaussian diameter (JRES Table 2). Phan/IMMI give 85 um D4-sigma contour / 100 um defocused infill; AMB2022-04 gives 80 um D4-sigma. Conflict B2 in PREREQUISITES.md - state the metric used.

layer_bands._comment: Z values verbatim from the paper text; layer indices from Table 3/4 band labels.

overhang.interpolation_rule: for layers 252-349, feature lengths interpolate linearly between layer 250 and layer 350 (verbatim table note)

bridge.cross_section: single merged feature spanning the part

ridges.note: NOT covered by any timing table in the paper. 11 ridges, 1 mm wide, 7 mm pitch (geometry from STL). Timing unpublished.

contour_timing_table3._comment: Laser-on duration per feature contour, ms. Same strategy odd and even layers. Contour order and start position varied per layer; time between leg contours varied 15.5-25.5 ms depending on travel.

infill_odd_layers_table4._comment: Odd layers: scan lines parallel to x, back and forth. First line starts at the upper-left corner of the part, in L1, travelling +x, hopping feature to feature (laser off) along constant y until the far end (base), then the direction reverses.
infill_odd_layers_table4.between_features_note: 1.66 ms measured for layers 1-250; overhang layers not measured, line-end 0.48 ms assumed unchanged (verbatim assumption in paper)

infill_even_layers_table5._comment: Even layers: scan lines parallel to y. First line starts at the lower-left corner of the part, travelling +y. Each feature is COMPLETED before the laser moves to the next feature (unlike odd layers, which hop per line). Scan direction alternates continuously. Lines start/end 0.03 mm from the bottom/top edges.

base.verdict: PAPER MISPRINT, verified 2026-07-28. Positional PDF reconstruction confirms the printed table does say 49, but geometry contradicts it: the base spans 16.5-19.0 mm in x, so y-parallel lines at 0.10 mm hatch give ~165-190 lines. The leg rows of this same table (49/50, 4/5, 24/25 lines for 5.0/0.5/2.5 mm widths) match width/hatch exactly, validating the column semantics; base, overhang and bridge rows carry a filled-down 49. Path generator must derive line counts as ceil(feature_x_width/hatch), never from these cells. The 0.00-5.00 width range and 0.01-6.25 ms per-line range are REAL: the part's right end is a 45-degree point in plan (max-x 72.55 at the y-edges to 75.00 at mid-y, confirmed at all heights in the STL), matching Fig 8's 'laser on time decreases in tip'.

bridge.verdict: same misprint as the base row: ~725-750 lines by geometry (72.5-75.0 mm / 0.10 mm hatch). Derive, do not copy.

infill_even_layers_table5.overhang_note: the layer-350 rows' printed 49 is likewise unreliable for even layers (e.g. thick legs 6.98 mm wide imply ~69 lines); derive from interpolated widths.

part_plan_geometry._comment: Verified from AMB2018_01_Part.STL by ray casting, 2026-07-28.
part_plan_geometry.right_end: 45-degree point in plan view: max-x = 72.55 mm at y = 0/5 edges rising linearly to 75.00 mm at y = 2.5 mid-plane; present at every height from the legs through the bridge (z 0.5 to 10 checked); the ridges stop at x = 71.0
part_plan_geometry.left_end: flat at x = 0 for all y
part_plan_geometry.consequence: the part is NOT an extrusion of its mid-plane cross-section; meshes and scan paths must model the tip. Odd-layer base scan-line lengths 16.49-18.94 mm and even-layer 0.00-4.94 mm both follow from this shape.

inter_part_and_layer.time_between_parts_note: from last infill line of one part to first contour of the next; varies with contour start position, which changed every layer
inter_part_and_layer.dwell: imposed at the end of each layer so the NIST AMMT (slower recoater) could replicate the build later (verbatim); duration not published separately - only the 52 s total and ~26 s scanning are given, and only for layers 1-250
inter_part_and_layer.layer_time_layers_251_plus_note: NOT PUBLISHED - gap E in PREREQUISITES.md

feature_id_map._comment: Feature labels vs geometry measured from AMB2018_01_Part.STL (left edge x, mm, at z=2.5). Widths: thick 5.0, thin 0.5, medium 2.5. The paper's L-numbering runs from the part's left end; the base is the 19 mm end block.
feature_id_map.note: mapping of L-labels to x positions is inferred from feature widths (L1/L4/L7/L10 thick, L2/L5/L8/L11 thin, L3/L6/L9/L12 medium) matching Table 4 lengths 5.0/0.5/2.5 mm; consistent with Fig 7 ordering L1 leftmost.
